clue.text: Legless amnesiacs knocked back bottles together

indicators.note: knocked back says the hidden letters are read backwards
the two words hold the letters inside them, the way a bottle holds a drink

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Drunks who can't remember anything down their bottles in one go.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'bottles together' as the definition, but 'bottles' is the containment signal: the phrase 'Legless amnesiacs' holds the letters. 'Together' alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: The French-derived phrase describes a group acting all at once as one body, which is what doing things jointly means.

clue.text: Thin gentlemen distilled the spirit of the 18th-century

indicators.note: distilling breaks a liquid down and refines it, so the letters of the two words are worked into a new order

explanation.surface: Spare, refined gentlemen are said to have captured the very essence of the eighteenth century.
explanation.definitionFit: The Age of Reason was the defining intellectual movement of Europe in the 1700s, so it was that century's spirit.

clue.text: Italian port, sadly on strike, demanding rise

indicators.note: in a down answer rising means the letters are read from the bottom up
in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the second

parts.note: alas is the sad exclamation
to ram is to strike hard

explanation.surface: Dock workers at an Italian port, unhappily on strike, are demanding a pay rise.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sicilian town on the western coast is a seaport, famous too for its fortified wine.

clue.text: Portly porter

definitions.meaning: portly means plump or heavily built
porter is a dark beer, and the strong dark beer of that family bears this name

explanation.surface: A heavy-set hotel porter.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means fat in one sense and names a dark beer close kin to porter in the other.

clue.text: Sirens for example in Crete's rocks

indicators.note: rocks is read as a verb, shaking the letters of the two words into a new order

explanation.surface: Mythical sirens luring sailors onto the rocky shores of Crete.
explanation.definitionFit: The Sirens of Greek myth lured sailors to their deaths with song, so they are tempters or seducers.

clue.text: How to make Eid pass quickly?

parts.note: read as an instruction, the answer tells you to take the word die and put it off, that is jumble it, which gives Eid

explanation.surface: A question about how to make the festival of Eid go by fast.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer, read as wordplay, is an instruction ('off' as an anagram signal) that turns DIE into EID.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb describes a population perishing one after another, a rapid passing away.

clue.text: Several footballers trying to get a free kick?

definitions.meaning: an old word meaning various or sundry

definitions.text: footballers trying to get a free kick?
definitions.meaning: players who throw themselves to the ground to win a foul

explanation.surface: A number of footballers trying to win a free kick.
explanation.definitionFit: The archaic adjective means various, and players who fake falls are mocked for taking a dive.

clue.text: Paranormal activity detected on path bordering a deserted coastal area

indicators.note: in a down clue the first piece sits on top of the rest

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is the classic paranormal faculty

indicators.note: the path runs round the outside of the other letters, forming their border

parts.note: a lane is a narrow path or road
D is a standard dictionary abbreviation for deserted

explanation.surface: Ghost-hunters pick up something spooky on a path beside an abandoned stretch of seaside.
explanation.definitionFit: A seafront promenade is a long open walkway along the shore of a resort.

clue.text: A Bit of Fry and Laurie, broadcast in Turkey

indicators.note: a bit of here means just the opening letter of the next word
broadcast is read as scattered, so the letters of the surname are spread into a new order

explanation.surface: The comedy sketch show A Bit of Fry and Laurie being shown on television in Turkey.
explanation.walkthrough: A Bit of Fry and Laurie was a BBC sketch show starring Stephen Fry and Hugh Laurie; the title hides the wordplay. 'Turkey' is not the country.
explanation.definitionFit: In show business a turkey is a flop, a production that bombs completely.

clue.text: He died like Pushkin having left more revolutionary verse, not originally accepted

indicators.note: the two outer letters take in the jumbled words, as a group accepts a newcomer
revolutionary means overturned, so the letters of the two words are turned into a new order
read with the word before it, the word is not as it originally was, so its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A Russian poet who, like Pushkin, was killed, leaving behind more radical poetry that was at first rejected.
explanation.walkthrough: Lermontov, like Pushkin, died in a duel. 'Not originally' is read as the word not out of its original order; the surface sense, 'at first rejected', hides that.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian Romantic poet was killed in a duel in 1841, four years after Pushkin met the same fate.

clue.text: Groom runs into bloke with girl

indicators.note: the letter goes into the middle of the other word

parts.note: a man who keeps a girl working the streets, a procurer
R is the cricket abbreviation for runs

explanation.surface: A bridegroom dashes in to meet a man accompanied by a young woman.
explanation.definitionFit: To groom oneself is to tidy and smarten up, which is the fussing over appearance this verb describes.

clue.text: Under pressure, attractive dish Tina Gomez works at top speed

parts.note: a pie is a baked dish

indicators.note: works means operates on, so the letters of the name are worked into a new order

parts.note: c, the speed of light, is the highest speed there is

explanation.surface: A glamorous Tina Gomez, under pressure, works flat out.
explanation.definitionFit: The physics term describes a material that becomes magnetic when stressed, so it attracts when squeezed.

clue.text: Former president offers financial help

definitions.meaning: Ulysses S. ... was the eighteenth US president
money awarded for a purpose, such as a student's award

explanation.surface: An ex-president offering money to help out.
explanation.definitionFit: The surname of the Civil War general turned president is also the word for a sum of money awarded.

clue.text: Dog, very old, with head dropped and arching

parts.note: a cur is a mongrel dog

indicators.note: the first letter of the word for old is removed

parts.note: mature means grown old

explanation.surface: A very elderly dog, its head drooping and its back arched.
explanation.definitionFit: Bending into a curve is what arching is, so the noun for a bend serves for the gerund.

clue.text: Teachers posing riddles, but not initially

indicators.note: the first letter of the sieves word is left off

parts.note: a riddle is a coarse sieve, so riddles are sieves

explanation.surface: Schoolteachers setting puzzles for their class.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Riddles' looks like puzzles, but a riddle is also a coarse sieve for soil or gravel.
explanation.definitionFit: Coaches and instructors teach skills, so they are teachers of a practical kind.

clue.text: Nothing could be better

parts.note: the phrase reads like praise of perfection, but taken literally it is about nothing at all, not even a tiny piece

explanation.walkthrough: The surface sounds like high praise; the answer is a phrase meaning nothing whatever, with 'scrap' a fragment and also a fight that a better might wager on.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means none at all, so it is an emphatic way of saying nothing.

clue.text: One type of bomb "will" get a ban? "Must" is what I mean

parts.note: the H-bomb, the hydrogen bomb, gives its letter
a veto is an official ban or block

explanation.surface: Someone explaining their words: does 'will' mean a bomb will be banned? No, they meant 'must'.
explanation.definitionFit: The two-word phrase expresses obligation, exactly the force of the modal verb.

clue.text: RLS novel with every other character involved in scandal (including a threesome)

indicators.note: the alternate letters take the other piece inside them
only alternate letters of the word are kept, starting from the second

parts.note: a trio is a group of three

explanation.surface: A Robert Louis Stevenson novel in which everyone is caught up in a scandal, a threesome among them.
explanation.definitionFit: Stevenson's 1893 novel, the sequel to Kidnapped, is titled after its heroine.

clue.text: It's the state to be in when there's sun and fresh air, they say

definitions.text: It's the state to be in when there's sun

indicators.note: they say means the words are spoken and heard, not spelt

parts.note: fresh means new and an air is a tune or ditty, so the phrase is new ditty

explanation.surface: Naturists explain the ideal state for enjoying sunshine and fresh air.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fresh air' looks like part of the sunbathing picture; it is the wordplay, a new song.
explanation.definitionFit: Being undressed is the condition many prefer for sunbathing, a light-hearted definition rather than a dictionary one.

clue.text: To decline support is more crazy

parts.note: to dip is to go down or decline
a pier is a supporting pillar of a bridge

explanation.surface: Someone thinks turning down help is madder still.
explanation.definitionFit: Dippy means silly or a bit mad, and the comparative form means sillier.

clue.text: A shrub used in some cigarettes — almost everyone recoiled after inhaling one

indicators.note: the reversed piece comes after the cigarette brand

parts.note: Camel is a brand of cigarettes

indicators.note: the reversed letters breathe in the numeral, holding it inside
recoiling is springing back, so the shortened word is read backwards
the last letter of the word for everyone is dropped

parts.note: all means everyone
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A shrub smoked in some cigarettes made nearly everyone recoil after one drag.
explanation.definitionFit: The glossy-leaved flowering evergreen from East Asia is a garden bush, kin to the tea plant.

clue.text: Continued to tell story with breaks for short rest

indicators.note: the letter breaks into the phrase, splitting it

parts.note: to lie on is to go on telling falsehoods, so this is lied on

explanation.surface: A storyteller kept going, pausing now and then for a brief rest.
explanation.definitionFit: The hyphenated noun is a nap or brief spell lying on a bed, a short rest.

clue.text: Sturdy farm animals at back of butchery

parts.note: livestock, or stock, are the animals kept on a farm

indicators.note: only the closing letter of the word is taken

explanation.surface: Robust farm animals waiting behind the butcher's shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Thickset and solidly built is what a sturdy, compact person or animal looks like.

clue.text: Former model's sorry about interpreter

parts.note: ex means former

indicators.note: the word for sorry goes round the model's job

parts.note: sorry means poor, as in a sorry state
a model sits for an artist; the 's is read as is, linking the pieces

explanation.surface: An ex-model apologises about an interpreter.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who expounds a text explains its meaning, which is what an interpreter does.

clue.text: Description of alternative energy mostly

indicators.note: an alternative arrangement of the letters is a new order
mostly means all but the last letter of the word

explanation.surface: A word that usually describes renewable power.
explanation.definitionFit: Environmentally friendly power from wind or sun is commonly labelled by this colour, which is exactly how alternative energy is described.

clue.text: Soldier drills regularly in April, May, June, etc

parts.note: GI is an American soldier

indicators.note: regularly means every second letter is taken

explanation.surface: A soldier runs drills at regular intervals through the spring months.
explanation.walkthrough: The months look like the definition's subject; they are given names for women.
explanation.definitionFit: April, May and June are all female first names, so they are examples of young women.

clue.text: It's Marx's birthplace, one hears

definitions.meaning: Karl Marx was born in this German city on the Moselle
one who hears and judges a case in court

explanation.surface: Someone is told that a place is where Karl Marx was born.
explanation.walkthrough: 'One hears' looks like a sound signal, but it is a second definition: someone who hears and decides a case.
explanation.definitionFit: The German city was Marx's home town, and the same spelling names a person who tries a legal case.

clue.text: Chaplain frequently drinks old Irish liquor, principally in church gallery

indicators.note: the outer pieces take in the others, as a drinker takes in liquid

parts.note: CH is an abbreviation for chaplain
oft is an old word for often

indicators.note: principally means only the leading letter of the word

explanation.surface: A chaplain often downs old Irish whiskey, mainly up in the church gallery.
explanation.definitionFit: The raised gallery where the singers sit in a church is named after the choir it holds.

clue.text: Astrophysicist taking pot

indicators.note: the long word takes the answer into itself, holding it among its letters

explanation.surface: A scientist who studies stars is caught smoking cannabis.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Pot' looks like cannabis; it is a cup won as a prize.
explanation.definitionFit: Sports slang calls a cup or prize won a pot, so the silverware is a trophy.

clue.text: Catherine's replaced the missing element

indicators.note: replaced means put back in a different place, so the remaining letters are rearranged
the little word is missing from the name, taken out of it

explanation.surface: Catherine has replaced the missing part of something.
explanation.definitionFit: The poisonous metalloid with atomic number 33 is one of the chemical elements.
